pages.intro:
Order Desk takes customer orders off your team's hands. Here is what it does with every order:

1. **Reads the order.** Emails, PDFs, spreadsheets and scans are all fine.
2. **Finds the customer** and matches each line to your product list.
3. **Applies that customer's rules**, such as full cartons only or a usual delivery day.
4. **Checks its own work** and flags anything it is not sure about.
5. **Asks a person to approve.** Nothing goes to the warehouse until someone says yes.

You stay in charge. Order Desk does the typing and the checking.
pages.title: Meet Order Desk

pages.description: Safe choices are already filled in. You can change any of these later on the Setup page.
pages.intro: Every business answers these a little differently. If you are not sure, leave them as they are.
pages.title: How should it handle orders?

pages.intro:
**Approve or reject.** Orders that are ready wait for you under *Waiting for you* on the Order Desk page. Open one to see the order lines, what was flagged and the original order, then approve or reject it.

**Fix what is wrong.** If a line is wrong, correct the order before you approve. Order Desk remembers the correction for next time.

**Keep the lists current.** Order Desk works from your product list and your customer list. When they change, upload the new file.
pages.title: What your team does

pages.intro:
Once Order Desk is turned on, open its **Files** tab. Two folders are waiting there.

**Lists.** Drop your lists here first: products, customers, delivery addresses and the customer catalogue. CSV or Excel, in any order. Each file loads by itself and shows up as a short job that says how many rows were loaded. When a list changes, upload the new file.

**Orders.** Drop customer orders here. Each file becomes one order, and Order Desk starts work on it straight away.

That is all. Press **Continue** to check your choices and install.
pages.title: After setup: two folders

pages.description: Already filled in with safe choices. Change these only if you need to.
pages.intro:
These are set for you and most teams never change them.

**Extra checks.** How far above a customer's usual quantity is worth a second look, how long the same PO number counts as a duplicate, whether substitutions are ever allowed, and what to do when a line has no unit.

**Budget and quiet hours.** How much AI the agent may use each month, and the hours it should not work.
